mode_note: Per recipe-feature-pipeline SKILL.md, the three-option enumeration invariant from substrate-translation-knowledge does NOT apply here. Each decision enumerates as many options as genuinely exist (1-N) with explicit rationale for option count. Single-option decisions are acceptable when a credible 'no alternatives considered because...' rationale exists.

substrate_context.secrets_surface: GitHub Codespaces secrets (EXA_API_KEY, CONTEXT7_API_KEY, TFE_TOKEN, etc.)
substrate_context.agent_surface: 36 .claude/agents/*.md files, zero existing mcp__ namespace usage
substrate_context.repo_composition: 73.8% markdown, ~52 python audit scripts as the LSP-symbol-rich surface

mappings.option_count_rationale: Four genuinely distinct posture options exist in the devcontainer substrate (Dockerfile RUN, devcontainer features, onCreate, postCreate). A fifth 'hybrid' is the credible recommended path because the five disjoint install mechanisms map onto different layers cleanly. Each option has independent merit; none is a straw-man.

options.name: hybrid_features_plus_postcreate
options.description: Devcontainer features for runtimes and CLIs that have first-party features (Node via ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/node, github-cli, Go toolchain via ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/go). postCreateCommand idempotent script for the 7 MCP-server installs (uvx Serena, npx mcp-openapi-schema, go install actionlint-mcp, binary fetch Terraform MCP, uvx/npx GitNexus). No project Dockerfile changes beyond what's already in place.

cost.maintenance_burden: low - features pin LTS; postCreate script is the single touchpoint for server inventory
cost.irreversibility_cost: low - both layers are two-way reversible

options.rationale: Pushes transient/idempotent work into postCreate (where re-run is safe), keeps stable runtime provisioning in features (where ghcr handles versioning), avoids re-litigating the E-0081 Dockerfile-Yarn-key failure mode. Single coherent path with per-server overrides as exceptions.

per_server_overrides.Terraform MCP (pre-built binary): wget + sha256sum verification inside postCreate; not a feature
per_server_overrides.actionlint-mcp (go install): uses Go toolchain provided by feature; postCreate invokes 'go install @<sha>'

options.name: dockerfile_bake_everything
options.description: Add all 7 MCP-server installs as RUN layers in a project-owned Dockerfile, producing a single baked image.

cost.maintenance_burden: high - every server bump requires image rebuild and re-push
cost.irreversibility_cost: medium - image rollback is straightforward but cache-invalidation is slow

options.rationale: Already-broken-once posture on this base image (E-0081 stale-Yarn apt key). Mixed package managers (uvx, npx, go install, binary) inflate Dockerfile complexity. Slow developer feedback (full rebuild for any change).

options.name: features_only
options.description: Author or use ghcr-hosted devcontainer features for every MCP server.

cost.maintenance_burden: high - we own seven feature repos
cost.irreversibility_cost: high - other consumers may adopt the features

options.rationale: No upstream features exist for 6 of 7 servers. Authoring + maintaining them is grossly disproportionate to the value vs. a postCreate script.

options.name: postcreate_for_everything
options.description: Use only postCreateCommand for runtimes (Node, Go) AND MCP servers, skipping features entirely.

cost.runtime_overhead: moderate - every container create reinstalls runtimes
cost.maintenance_burden: medium - we maintain version-pinning logic the features already handle

options.rationale: Re-invents what ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/node and /go give us for free. Slower create-time and no benefit.

mappings.recommended_summary: Hybrid: ghcr.io/devcontainers/features for Node + Go + github-cli, postCreateCommand idempotent script for the 7 MCP-server installs, with per-server overrides for the binary and go-install cases.

mappings.option_count_rationale: Per-server-stdio vs per-server-remote where vendor offers it. 'All stdio' or 'all remote' are pseudo-options because 5 of 7 are stdio-native (no remote endpoint exists) and 2 of 7 have vendor-canonical remote endpoints. The real decision degenerates to a per-server table.

options.name: per_server_vendor_canonical
options.description: Per-server transport selection based on what each vendor canonically publishes.

cost.maintenance_burden: low - .mcp.json is the single declaration site

options.rationale: Aligns each server with its vendor-supported transport. Lets HTTP servers (Context7, Exa) inherit Claude Code's 5-attempt exponential-backoff auto-reconnect (C-0300/C-0302). Stdio servers cover the no-network-egress case and bypass SaaS availability dependencies.

options.name: all_stdio_with_local_fallback_binaries
options.description: Run local fallback binaries for Context7 and Exa as well.

cost.maintenance_burden: high - we track upstream local-binary releases for two vendors that prefer SaaS

options.rationale: Loses Claude Code's stdio-no-reconnect (C-0301) safety net of HTTP auto-reconnect. Forces us to maintain local-fallback infra for vendor-SaaS-canonical surfaces. No benefit unless the user explicitly needs offline operation, which is not in scope.

mappings.recommended_summary: Per-server table: stdio for the 5 OSS-local servers (Serena, mcp-openapi-schema, actionlint-mcp, Terraform MCP, GitNexus); remote HTTP for the 2 SaaS-canonical servers (Context7, Exa).

mappings.option_count_rationale: Three credible provisioning mechanisms exist (devcontainer feature, NodeSource apt, nvm). Each is widely used in practice; selection is mostly about idiom-fit.

options.name: ghcr_node_feature
options.description: Add ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/node:1 with an explicit LTS major pin (e.g., version: '20' for Node 20 LTS) to devcontainer.json.

cost.maintenance_burden: low - one frontmatter line; upstream feature handles apt/PPA mechanics

options.rationale: Declarative, ghcr-hosted, LTS-pinnable, idiomatic. Matches the precedent set by ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/github-cli already in use.

options.name: dockerfile_apt_nodesource
options.description: Add the NodeSource apt repo and install nodejs in a Dockerfile RUN layer.

cost.maintenance_burden: medium - we own the apt key + repo URL drift (E-0081 history)

options.rationale: Already-burned-on-apt-keys posture (E-0081). The feature pins LTS more cleanly with less code surface.

options.name: nvm_postcreate
options.description: Install nvm in Dockerfile, then run 'nvm install <lts>' in postCreate.

cost.maintenance_burden: medium - shell-rc plumbing required

options.rationale: nvm is right for multi-version Node workflows. We need one pinned LTS. Overkill.

mappings.recommended_summary: Add ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/node:1 with an explicit LTS major pin in devcontainer.json features block.

mappings.option_count_rationale: Four hook points exist (onCreate, postCreate, postStart, postAttach), but the FR-8 sub-tasks map onto them mechanically: install-time work goes in postCreate (runs once after create); readiness-probe work goes in postStart (runs every container start). onCreate is too early (no project mount for stdio servers needing repo context). postAttach is too late (user-visible delay). The real decision is whether to layer postCreate+postStart or pick one.

options.name: layered_postcreate_install_poststart_probe
options.description: postCreateCommand runs the idempotent install script and the initial install-verification ping for all 7 servers. postStartCommand runs a fast readiness probe (ping each server) and writes the result to .claude/runtime/mcp-events.jsonl. postAttachCommand is unused unless we need a user-facing greeting later.

cost.runtime_overhead: minor - probe loop on every container start (~7 pings, <2s)
cost.maintenance_burden: low - two hook scripts; each is small

options.rationale: Separates the once-per-create (install) work from the every-start (readiness) work. Captures both classes of FR-8 failure: install-time (postCreate) and start-time/transport (postStart). Aligns with claims attributing install completion to postCreate (C-0156/C-0240) and recurring readiness to postStart (C-0344/C-0367/C-0436).

hook_mapping.onCreateCommand: unused (too early for stdio servers needing project mount)
hook_mapping.postStartCommand: readiness probe of all 7 servers, write event to mcp-events.jsonl, non-fatal on transient failures

options.name: single_poststart_only
options.description: Put both install and probe in postStartCommand.

cost.runtime_overhead: significant - reinstall checks every container start
cost.maintenance_burden: medium

options.rationale: Conflates two distinct failure modes. Slow every-start cycle. Risks masking install-time failures when a postStart re-run silently passes.

mappings.recommended_summary: postCreateCommand for install + verification; postStartCommand for readiness probe writing to mcp-events.jsonl; onCreate and postAttach unused.

mappings.option_count_rationale: C-0349 explicitly verifies 'NO CONSENSUS PATTERN' across 5 source categories. Three options are surfaced verbatim in the corpus (stderr banner, dedicated jsonl event file, agent-level acknowledgement). A fourth (frontmatter convention) is added because ADR-0018 already codifies primary/fallback semantics in agent frontmatter and a structured convention there is the cheapest way to make the transition machine-readable without inventing a runtime event surface. Genuine novel-design space, four genuine options.

options.name: combined_jsonl_plus_stderr_banner
options.description: Primary surface: append a structured JSON record to .claude/runtime/mcp-events.jsonl on every primary-to-fallback transition (event type 'primary_degraded', fields: timestamp, primary_server, fallback_server, reason, agent). Secondary surface: a one-line stderr banner from whichever MCP component detects the transition (ephemeral operator hint). Agents do NOT need to acknowledge in their own output — the jsonl is the contract.

cost.maintenance_burden: low - schema lives in KB-mcp-design
cost.irreversibility_cost: medium - .jsonl event-shape is a first-time convention; future consumers may grow

options.rationale: Combines the strengths of (a) ephemeral and (b) machine-readable. The jsonl gives FR-9 a structured-failure-record handle; the stderr banner gives an operator a visible 'using fallback' cue without forcing every agent to template-print the same string. Avoids uniformity risk of option (c) across 36 agents.

options.name: jsonl_only
options.description: Only the mcp-events.jsonl event file; no stderr surface.

cost.maintenance_burden: low

options.rationale: Operator-invisible until someone tails the file. Loses the ephemeral hint cheaply provided by stderr.

options.name: stderr_banner_only
options.description: Only the stderr banner; no structured event.

cost.maintenance_burden: low

options.rationale: Loses machine-readability. FR-9's structured-failure-record requirement falls back on ad-hoc stderr parsing — brittle.

options.name: agent_level_acknowledgement
options.description: Each agent prints a 'using fallback' line in its own output when it detects primary degradation.

cost.maintenance_burden: high - 36 agents must adopt the convention uniformly
cost.irreversibility_cost: high - retrofitting a different convention requires editing 36 files

options.rationale: Uniformity risk (C-0357). 36 agents adopting a free-text convention will drift. The runtime surface should be runtime-owned, not agent-owned.

options.name: frontmatter_convention_only
options.description: Encode primary/fallback in agent frontmatter (declarative); rely on agent to read its own frontmatter at startup and emit on transition.

cost.maintenance_burden: high - every agent author owns the convention

options.rationale: Declarative-only; still doesn't solve the transition-event surface. Frontmatter remains useful for declaring primary/fallback pairs (ADR-0018) but is not a transition-surfacing mechanism.

mappings.recommended_summary: Append structured JSON record to .claude/runtime/mcp-events.jsonl on every primary->fallback transition, paired with a one-line stderr banner from the runtime detector. Agents do not template-print; the jsonl is the FR-9 contract.

mappings.option_count_rationale: Three credible surfaces map onto the seven-server reality: stderr (the spec-default, auto-captured by Claude Code per C-0314), the shared mcp-events.jsonl (UI-15 alignment), and MCP protocol-level notifications/message (logging/setLevel from the spec). Per-server file logs and a proxy/supervisor were enumerated in the frame but are rejected on operational complexity grounds.

options.name: stderr_default_plus_mcp_events_jsonl_for_transitions
options.description: All 7 servers log to stderr (the MCP-spec default for stdio; HTTP servers' logs come through Claude Code's HTTP client logging). Claude Code captures stderr automatically (C-0314). The shared .claude/runtime/mcp-events.jsonl is reserved for cross-server event correlation (UI-15 transitions, FR-8 readiness probe results, FR-9 structured failure records) — NOT a per-line log mirror.

cost.runtime_overhead: minor - jsonl append on coarse events only
cost.maintenance_burden: low

options.rationale: Aligns with MCP spec (C-0313 'should not stdout for stdio'), gets auto-capture for free (C-0314), and reserves the structured jsonl for actually-structured events. Composes cleanly with D-0005 (transitions) and D-0008 (probes).

options.name: structured_json_stderr_per_server
options.description: Require every server to emit structured JSON on stderr (machine-parseable).

cost.maintenance_burden: high - 7 upstream servers don't agree on log format

options.rationale: We don't control 7 upstream log formats. Forcing structured stderr requires wrapping each server in a json-reformatter. Disproportionate to value.

options.name: proxy_supervisor_toolhive_style
options.description: Run a ToolHive-style proxy/supervisor (E-0085) that intercepts every MCP transport and uniformly instruments logs.

cost.runtime_overhead: significant - long-running process between Claude Code and every server
cost.maintenance_burden: high - new long-running component to monitor

options.rationale: Adds a new long-running process whose crash blast-radius is wider than the seven it's wrapping. Out-of-proportion for FR-10.

mappings.recommended_summary: Stderr default for per-server logs (auto-captured by Claude Code); mcp-events.jsonl reserved for coarse-grained structured events (transitions, probe results, structured failure records).

mappings.option_count_rationale: Single-option decision with credible no-alternatives rationale. The .mcp.json env: block already declares which env vars are credentials (EXA_API_KEY, CONTEXT7_API_KEY, TFE_TOKEN); deriving the redaction allowlist from that block is the canonical single-source-of-truth approach. Per-server redaction config (option B in the frame) duplicates the declaration; sink-side redaction (option C) defers to log infra we don't control; header-name redaction (option D) is a sub-task within the recommended option, not a competing one. OWASP MCP01 (C-0333) does not prescribe a mechanism — it prescribes the property.

options.name: redact_at_source_env_var_name_allowlist
options.description: At the log-surface boundary (the layer that reads stderr from each MCP server and writes to host logs), apply a redaction filter keyed on the env-var NAMES declared in .mcp.json's env: block plus HTTP-header names for HTTP transports (CONTEXT7_API_KEY-equivalent headers, Authorization, x-api-key). Replace matched values with the literal '[REDACTED:<envvar>]'. Reject Exa's exaApiKey query-param URL form (E-0095) at .mcp.json validation time, not at log time.

cost.runtime_overhead: minor - regex match per log line
cost.maintenance_burden: low - adding a new credential adds one line to .mcp.json and the redaction list rebuilds

options.rationale: Single source of truth (.mcp.json env: block); addresses OWASP MCP01 (C-0333) directly; rejects URL-embedded-credential anti-pattern at config time (E-0095); composes with secret-via-env-only invocation discipline to mitigate argv-leakage (E-0094, which cannot be fixed at log layer alone). Sink-side redaction at log-aggregator layer is rejected because we don't ship one; per-server redaction config is rejected because it duplicates .mcp.json.

mappings.no_alternatives_rationale: All four corpus options reduce to either 'redact at source from a single declarative inventory' or non-options (deferring to non-existent log infra; duplicating the .mcp.json declaration in per-server configs). Header-name redaction for HTTP transports is folded into the recommended option as a sub-mechanism.
mappings.recommended_summary: Redact at the log-surface boundary using an allowlist derived from .mcp.json env: var names plus HTTP-transport header names; reject URL-embedded credentials at config validation time.

mappings.option_count_rationale: MCP JSON-RPC ping (spec-canonical, transport-agnostic) vs claude mcp list output parsing (host-side, no spec dependency but brittle). HTTP /health endpoint is rejected upfront (HTTP-only, doesn't generalize). Real tool-call probes are rejected upfront (uneven side-effects across servers). The two surviving options are real and meaningfully different.

options.name: json_rpc_ping_plus_optional_probe
options.description: Use the MCP-spec JSON-RPC ping (E-0027, C-0290/C-0291) as the canonical readiness primitive in postStartCommand. For the 2 HTTP servers (Context7, Exa) where ping succeeds without validating auth, supplement with one explicit authenticated read-only probe call (Context7: resolve-library-id with a known id; Exa: web_search_exa with a trivial query) gated behind an environment flag so probes can be disabled when API quotas matter.

cost.runtime_overhead: minor - 7 ping calls + 2 optional probes at every container start
cost.maintenance_burden: low - ping is spec-stable

options.rationale: Spec-canonical (C-0290/C-0291), transport-agnostic, endorsed by Fast.io monitoring guidance (E-0107, C-0295/C-0296). Probe supplement addresses the 'ping doesn't validate auth' risk surfaced in the frame for Context7/Exa with bad API keys. Stays within a one-shot lifecycle hook (no active ping-loop supervisor E-0084).

options.name: claude_mcp_list_parsing
options.description: Run 'claude mcp list' and parse output to determine each server's connection state.

cost.maintenance_burden: high - brittle to Claude Code CLI output format changes

options.rationale: Brittle host-side CLI scraping. Tightly coupled to Claude Code's output format with no SemVer contract.

mappings.recommended_summary: Use MCP JSON-RPC ping for all 7 servers in postStartCommand; supplement with an authenticated read-only probe for Context7 and Exa to validate API-key correctness (env-flag-gated for quota-sensitive runs).

mappings.option_count_rationale: Single-option decision with credible no-alternatives rationale. The mapping is determined by consumer roles already documented in agent frontmatter and per-agent consumer claims (E-0057..E-0060). 'Narrow per-agent' vs 'broad wildcard' frame options are not real alternatives — broad wildcard fails the least-privilege principle that the existing 36 agents already follow with their tools allowlist. The decision IS the table.

options.name: per_agent_narrow_allowlist_driven_by_consumer_claims
options.description: Each agent's tools allowlist gets exactly the mcp__<server>__<tool> entries its role requires. Non-consumers get no MCP tools added.

cost.maintenance_burden: medium - 36 agent files have frontmatter edits; per-tool granularity requires the team to track tool-id changes (e.g., Context7 v1.2.0 ReplaceContentTool replaces ReplaceRegexTool)

options.rationale: Aligns with existing tools-allowlist precedent in the 36 agents (zero existing mcp__ usage, C-0445, is the starting point). Least-privilege; minimizes the set of agents that break on tool-id changes. The mapping itself is mechanical from consumer claims.

mapping_table.Serena: deferred to D-0013 outcome (full / narrowed to ~6 audit-script-touching agents / drop)
mapping_table.all_other_agents: no mcp__ entries (zero existing usage preserved)

mappings.no_alternatives_rationale: 'Broad wildcard' violates the existing least-privilege convention; 'narrow per-agent' is the convention. The remaining work is producing the table, which is determined by consumer claims, not a design choice.
mappings.recommended_summary: Per-agent narrow allowlist driven by consumer claims. Serena entries are conditional on D-0013.

mappings.option_count_rationale: Single-option decision with credible no-alternatives rationale. Three existing W/H/A trifectas pass review and follow a consistent convention (ADR-0020 frontmatter, sister-cross-reference convention, body-prose family membership, ADR-0030 pedagogical_sections). Varying the convention for the MCP trifecta would create a 4th template to maintain with zero offsetting benefit. The 'KB-codespaces stub' option in the frame is not a real alternative — a stub is a temporary state, not a convention to copy.

options.name: follow_kb_cc_platform_template_verbatim
options.description: Author KB-mcp-platform/SKILL.md and KB-mcp-design/SKILL.md following KB-cc-platform + KB-cc-design template verbatim: ADR-0020 frontmatter, ADR-0030 pedagogical_sections, sister-cross-reference convention (auditing-mcp <-> KB-mcp-platform/design), body-prose family membership. Resolve the family-coordinator conflict (E-0044 vs E-0049, auditing-mcp currently lives in auditing-cc-configs family per C-0460) by either (a) graduating auditing-mcp to its own family with KB-mcp-platform/design as its sister halves, or (b) keeping auditing-mcp in auditing-cc-configs and treating KB-mcp-platform/design as sibling knowledge skills with explicit cross-refs. The Synthesizer should surface this family-coordinator question to the user before authoring.

cost.maintenance_burden: low - same review cadence as other trifectas

options.rationale: Three existing trifectas pass review (C-0466/C-0470/C-0471 etc.). No reason to vary. Honors ADR-0030 pedagogical_sections (E-0078, C-0528). Fixes the broken sister-cross-reference (auditing-mcp -> non-existent KB-mcp-* halves).

mappings.no_alternatives_rationale: The KB-codespaces template is itself a degraded stub-precedent (auditing-codespaces is a STUB per ADR-0033); copying it would be copying a known-incomplete pattern. Custom MCP-specific structure deviates from convention with no offsetting benefit.
mappings.recommended_summary: Follow KB-cc-platform + KB-cc-design template verbatim; resolve family-coordinator question (auditing-mcp graduates to its own family, or remains in auditing-cc-configs with KB-mcp-* as sibling skills) before authoring.

mappings.option_count_rationale: Three policy stances exist: exact-tag-where-available + commit-SHA-fallback, vendor-controlled-latest, floating-minor. Each is in real use somewhere in the broader devcontainer ecosystem; the choice is determined by reproducibility appetite and upstream release shape.

options.name: exact_tag_or_commit_sha_per_server
options.description: Per-server pinning where each server's pin form is driven by its upstream release shape. Exact tag where releases exist (Serena, mcp-openapi-schema, Terraform MCP, Context7, GitNexus). Commit SHA where no tags exist (actionlint-mcp via 'go install <repo>@<sha>', C-0133/C-0153). Pin-then-review discipline (E-0074) is mandatory: every supply-chain bump goes through audit.

cost.maintenance_burden: medium - periodic supply-chain review cadence

options.rationale: Already the established convention in the repo (E-0073). Honors deterministic-install for FR-2/FR-3. Pin-then-review caught Serena v1.3.0 base_modes->added_modes breaking change (E-0098) and Context7 v1.2.0 ReplaceContentTool tool-id change (E-0097).

per_server_pin.Serena: exact tag (e.g., v1.2.x where v1.3.0 breaking change is under review)
per_server_pin.actionlint-mcp: commit SHA via go install (no tags exist, C-0133/C-0153)
per_server_pin.Terraform MCP: exact tag matching pre-built-binary release asset
per_server_pin.Context7: vendor-controlled at remote endpoint; for the .mcp.json client, pin to the API version header where available
per_server_pin.Exa: vendor-controlled at remote endpoint; pin client SDK by tag if applicable

options.name: vendor_controlled_latest
options.description: Let each upstream/registry resolve to latest at install time.

cost.maintenance_burden: low until something breaks, then catastrophic

options.rationale: Non-reproducible. Already-witnessed breakage (E-0098 Serena, E-0097 Context7) demonstrates this policy fails open.

options.name: floating_minor
options.description: Pin to major.x (e.g., 1.x) and float minor versions.

cost.maintenance_burden: medium

options.rationale: Some upstreams (mcp-openapi-schema 0.0.1) have no minor range. Inconsistent applicability across the seven.

mappings.recommended_summary: Exact-tag pin where releases exist; commit-SHA pin for actionlint-mcp (no tags); periodic supply-chain review on every bump.

mappings.option_count_rationale: Two real options: bump the ADR to v1.1.0 (codifying the blast-radius extension in the ADR) vs. clarify in the ADR that v1.1.0 SHAPE lives in KB-codebase-research and ADR remains the v1.0.0 contract. Status-quo defer is rejected upfront (the frame already labels it 'not recommended; documented drift'). Adjacent ADR-0007 relocation is a separate small task, not a competing option.

options.name: bump_adr_0018_to_v_1_1_0
options.description: Bump ADR-0018 schema_version frontmatter and the JSON example body to 1.1.0; add a section explicitly documenting the blast-radius extension. Add a 'schema-version history' table to the ADR. Update the two downstream consumers (discovery-codebase-researcher, review-architecture-auditor) to validate against v1.1.0. Also relocate or cross-reference ADR-0007 from adrs-migrated/ to adrs/ as a small adjacent fix (E-0080, low severity).

cost.maintenance_burden: low - ADR is the contract; KB stays as guidance

options.rationale: Eliminates the drift at its source. The ADR is the contract; making it match the actual KB-and-agent reality removes ambiguity. Closes the latent landmine (C-0496) by making the schema_version field unambiguous everywhere.

options.name: clarify_in_adr_kb_is_v_1_1_0_source
options.description: Keep ADR-0018 at v1.0.0; add a cross-reference clarifying that v1.1.0 SHAPE is described in KB-codebase-research.

cost.maintenance_burden: medium - readers must follow a cross-reference to find the canonical shape

options.rationale: Splits the contract across two documents. Future bumps would need the same dance. ADRs exist to be the contract; the KB shouldn't carry contract-grade material the ADR disclaims.

mappings.recommended_summary: Bump ADR-0018 to v1.1.0; codify blast-radius extension; update two downstream consumers to validate v1.1.0; relocate/cross-reference ADR-0007 adjacent.

mappings.option_count_rationale: Three genuinely distinct postures: full always-on (broad surface for all 36 agents), narrowed always-on (allowlisted to specific agents like the ones touching the 52 Python audit scripts), drop entirely (GitNexus fills the code-graph slot). Each has real cost/benefit tradeoffs given the 73.8% markdown finding and the GitNexus-as-canonical-primary status.

options.name: narrowed_always_on_python_audit_surface_only
options.description: Keep Serena in .mcp.json (always-on at the project level) but restrict mcp__serena__* tool entries in the 36 agent allowlists to only those whose role actually touches Python code: review-architecture-auditor (audit-script-related symbol lookups), the design-* agents that touch tooling Python, and any code-spelunking discovery agent. Markdown-dominant agents get no Serena tools. Pin to a pre-v1.3.0 tag while the base_modes->added_modes breaking change is reviewed (E-0098).

cost.runtime_overhead: minor - Serena process running but rarely invoked
cost.maintenance_burden: medium - Serena breaking-change history (E-0098) requires periodic review
cost.irreversibility_cost: low - can drop later by removing one .mcp.json entry and ~6 agent frontmatter lines

options.rationale: 73.8% markdown (C-0485) means Serena's LSP-symbol value-prop is narrow but non-zero. The 52 Python audit scripts (C-0490, verified) are the real symbol-rich surface and benefit from Serena. GitNexus is the canonical code-graph primary (ADR-0007 v2.2.0, E-0038) for repository-graph queries; Serena complements it for in-file LSP lookups. C-0449 explicitly hedges 'symbol-level value contingent on UI-8 narrowing' — narrowing IS the resolution.

options.name: full_always_on
options.description: Broad Serena tool surface available to all 36 agents.

cost.maintenance_burden: high - every agent inherits Serena's breaking-change blast-radius

options.rationale: Mismatch with 73.8% markdown corpus (C-0485). Most agents would never invoke a Serena tool but would carry its breaking-change risk. Violates least-privilege.

options.name: drop_from_always_on
options.description: Remove Serena from .mcp.json entirely; GitNexus fills the code-graph slot.

cost.maintenance_burden: low - Serena no longer in the surface
cost.irreversibility_cost: medium - reintroducing later requires re-litigating UI-8

options.rationale: Loses the LSP-symbol value-prop for the 52 Python audit-script surface where it genuinely helps. GitNexus is repo-graph-canonical, not in-file-LSP-canonical; the two are complementary, not substitutable. C-0449's 'contingent on UI-8 narrowing' implies narrowing was the expected path.

mappings.recommended_summary: Narrowed always-on: Serena in .mcp.json at project level; mcp__serena__* entries only in agents that touch the 52 Python audit scripts (review-architecture-auditor and the Python-touching design agents). Pin pre-v1.3.0 pending base_modes->added_modes review.
